posts.content:
The Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series is the first model to be finished with our award-winning PixelPaint technology, now running at the Mercedes-Benz AG plant in Sindelfingen.
 
PixelPaint applies paint through a print head instead of spraying it. There is no overspray, so every drop lands on the car. No masking, no rework, no paint lost to the air.
 
That precision is what makes individual finishes like the Monogram Series possible on a production line.

posts.content:
🏁 In racing, the fastest car doesn’t stay competitive by standing still. Neither does a robot.
A robot may still be mechanically productive years after installation, but the technology around it can quickly move on.

Changing production demands, shorter product cycles, cybersecurity, connectivity, new regulations and emerging technologies like AI all put new demands on existing automation.
That’s where modernization comes in.

Rather than replacing valuable assets, a phased modernization approach can help companies extend robot life, reduce operational risk and unlock new capabilities — keeping automation ready for the next challenge.

The goal isn’t simply to have newer technology. It’s to make sure the technology you already have continues to deliver business value.

🏎️ Keep the robots in the race. Keep improving.

posts.content:
We’ve all seen self-driving cars
But have you heard of a self-driving lab?

Meet Dunia Innovations, a Berlin-based company using AI and ABB robots to accelerate materials discovery.

At Dunia’s self-driving lab in Berlin, AI acts like the scientist’s co-pilot, learning from every trial in the experiment and proposing new formulations or protocols to follow. While AI is the brain behind the experiments, ABB Robotics’ GoFa cobot swiftly and accurately carries out the experimental workflow.

And the cycle repeats as the system continuously learns, adapts and determines protocols for the next test until - Eureka!

The continuous Design-Make-Test-Analyze loop carried out by robots is what we call a “Self-Driving Lab” and helps speed up experiments for applications such as producing green hydrogen or finding ways to re-use industrial carbon-dioxide emissions.

Dunia’s AI models are working to create a more sustainable energy environment, and ABB robots are putting their thoughts into action.

Watch the video below to learn more.

posts.content:
Keeping Cool Under Pressure: Protecting Your Robot Controllers from Heat

High temperatures are a challenge not just for people — but also for control
technology.

Robot controllers can generally handle elevated temperatures well, but once they
exceed 45°C, conditions can become critical. This can lead to premature wear or
even complete system failure. The Air Conditioning Kit for OmniCore V250 and
V400 robot controllers from ABB Robotics enables reliable operation in
demanding environments with temperatures of up to 55°C.

This is especially relevant for applications in foundries, forging plants, and other
environments exposed to high levels of dust and dirt. The closed-loop cooling
circuit provides enhanced protection against contamination inside the
controller, helping to prevent overheating and unplanned downtime.

The retrofit takes just a few hours and can be carried out either at the ABB
Robotics workshop in Friedberg or on-site at your facility.

Keep your automation running reliably — even in the most demanding conditions. Reach
out to us to find out how to prepare your OmniCore controller for high
temperatures and harsh operating environments.

Get in touch: https://lnkd.in/egpT-Rde
